stories.title: Geofence Zone CRUD Management
stories.user_story: As a platform operator, I want to create, read, update, and delete geofence zones with polygon/circle definitions, so that I can configure the areas where consumers receive location-triggered offers
acceptance_criteria: Given I am authenticated as a platform operator, When I create a zone with a valid GeoJSON polygon or centre+radius circle, Then the zone is persisted in PostGIS with a spatial index (GiST) and returns a unique zone_id
Given I submit a zone with fewer than 3 polygon vertices or radius < 50m or > 5000m, When I save, Then a 400 error is returned with a descriptive validation message
Given I update an existing zone's geometry, When the update is saved, Then the spatial index is rebuilt for that zone and active geofence monitors are notified within 60 seconds
Given I delete a zone that has active offers linked, When I attempt deletion, Then I receive a warning requiring confirmation and linked offers are deactivated upon confirm
Then all zone CRUD operations are audit-logged with operator_id, timestamp, and before/after geometry hashes
Then zone geometry data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3) as location data is classified Restricted
stories.regulatory_linkage: UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — integrity and confidentiality of location data
stories.reasoning: Core backend service enabling all geofencing. 5 points: PostGIS spatial schema + GiST indexing + CRUD API + validation + audit logging + cascading deactivation. Restricted because zone geometry combined with user presence reveals location patterns.

stories.title: Device-Side Geofence Monitoring (iOS/Android)
stories.user_story: As a consumer who has granted 'Always' location permission, I want my device to monitor geofence boundaries in the background, so that I receive relevant offers when I enter or exit a zone without draining my battery
acceptance_criteria: Given I have granted 'Always' location permission, When geofence zones are synced to my device, Then CLLocationManager (iOS) or GeofencingClient (Android) registers up to 100 active geofences

Given I physically enter a registered geofence zone, When the OS triggers an entry event, Then a geofence_entry event is published to the backend within 5 seconds including zone_id, timestamp, and anonymised device_id
Given I physically exit a registered geofence zone, When the OS triggers an exit event, Then a geofence_exit event is published to the backend within 5 seconds

Given the device has limited geofence slots, When more than 100 zones exist in my city, Then the app prioritises the nearest zones based on last-known location and rotates on significant location change
Given battery optimization is active, When monitoring geofences, Then background location usage does not exceed 2% battery per hour as measured by OS battery stats
Then location coordinates transmitted in geofence events are encrypted end-to-end and never stored in plaintext on device or in application logs
stories.regulatory_linkage: UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — data minimization (transmit zone_id + timestamp, not continuous GPS); GDPR Art. 25 — data protection by design
stories.reasoning: Dual-platform native implementation with OS-specific APIs. 5 points: CLLocationManager + GeofencingClient + zone prioritisation algorithm + battery optimization + encrypted event publishing. Restricted as real-time location data.

stories.title: Real-Time Offer Matching Pipeline
stories.user_story: As a consumer entering a geofence zone, I want to receive a relevant offer within 2 seconds of entry, so that I can act on time-sensitive deals while I am near the merchant
acceptance_criteria: Given a geofence_entry event is published to Pub/Sub, When the matching pipeline processes it, Then a matched offer (or no-match decision) is resolved within 2 seconds end-to-end (P95)

Given the pipeline receives an entry event, When filtering offers, Then only offers that match the zone, are within validity period, and align with the consumer's consent and preferences are considered
Given multiple offers match, When ranking, Then offers are scored by relevance (category preference weight × recency × merchant proximity) and the top offer is dispatched
Given the consumer has already redeemed or dismissed this offer in the past 7 days, When matching, Then that offer is suppressed and the next-best is selected
Given the pipeline cannot resolve within 2 seconds (timeout), When the SLA is breached, Then the event is dead-lettered for retry and a monitoring alert fires
Then all offer-matching decisions are logged with consumer_id (pseudonymised), zone_id, offers_considered, offer_selected, and latency_ms for audit
stories.regulatory_linkage: UK GDPR Art. 22 — right not to be subject to solely automated decision-making (offer matching must be explainable)

architecture_kb_sections: kb-L0-lloyds-enterprise-architecture §4.1 (Pub/Sub event bus, Dataflow stream processing)

stories.reasoning: Event-driven pipeline is the core real-time engine. 5 points: Pub/Sub consumer + filter logic + ranking algorithm + suppression rules + SLA enforcement + dead-letter + audit logging. Restricted because matching uses location + transaction preferences.

stories.title: Offer Dispatch via Push Notification
stories.user_story: As a consumer who has been matched with an offer, I want to receive a push notification with the offer summary, so that I am alerted even when the app is not in the foreground
acceptance_criteria: Given an offer has been matched and the consumer has push notifications enabled, When the offer is dispatched, Then a push notification is delivered within 1 second of dispatch containing merchant name, offer headline, and expiry
Given the consumer taps the notification, When the app opens, Then it deep-links directly to the offer detail screen with full terms visible
Given the consumer has push notifications disabled, When an offer is matched, Then the offer is silently added to the in-app feed without notification
Given a screen reader is active, When the notification is announced, Then it reads: '[Merchant name]: [Offer headline]. Tap to view details'
Given the consumer receives more than 3 offer notifications in a 1-hour window, When the 4th triggers, Then it is batched into a summary notification: 'You have X new offers nearby'
Then location event payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and user_id is hashed in all geofence event logs
stories.regulatory_linkage: Consumer Duty (PS22/9) — communications must be clear, fair, and not misleading
stories.reasoning: Notification is the primary delivery channel for real-time offers. 3 points: FCM/APNs integration + deep-linking + batching logic + accessibility. Confidential (not Restricted) as notification content is offer data, not raw location.

stories.title: In-App Offer Feed with Sort and Filter
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to browse a scrollable feed of available offers sorted by relevance, so that I can discover deals even when I haven't triggered a geofence
acceptance_criteria: Given I open the Offers tab, When the feed loads, Then I see a paginated list (20 items per page) of offers sorted by relevance score (proximity × preference match × recency) with infinite scroll
Given I apply a category filter (e.g., 'Food & Drink', 'Retail'), When the filter is active, Then only offers matching the selected categories are shown and the active filter count is displayed
Given I change sort order to 'Nearest', 'Newest', or 'Expiring soon', When I select a sort option, Then the feed re-orders accordingly within 500ms
Given I scroll past the last loaded page, When more offers exist, Then the next page loads seamlessly with a loading indicator; if no more exist, a 'You're all caught up' message appears
Given a screen reader is active, When navigating the feed, Then each offer card announces: merchant name, offer headline, distance, and expiry in that order
Given a screen reader is active, When I activate a filter or sort control, Then the updated result count is announced via a live region
Then raw GPS coordinates are not stored beyond the geofence match — only the zone_id and event_type are persisted
stories.regulatory_linkage: Consumer Duty (PS22/9) — fair presentation of offers without misleading prominence
stories.reasoning: Primary discovery surface for offers. 3 points: paginated API + sort/filter UI + infinite scroll + accessibility. Confidential as feed shows offer data personalised to user preferences but not raw location.

stories.title: Offer Feed Empty and Error States
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to see helpful messaging when no offers are available or when loading fails, so that I understand the situation and know what to do next
acceptance_criteria: Given I open the Offers tab and no offers are available in my area, When the feed loads, Then I see an empty state illustration with message 'No offers nearby right now. We'll notify you when new ones appear!' and a 'Browse all categories' CTA
Given I have applied filters that return zero results, When the empty state shows, Then the message reads 'No offers match your filters' with a 'Clear filters' button
Given the feed API returns a 5xx error or times out (>5s), When loading fails, Then I see an error state with 'Something went wrong' message and a 'Try again' button that retries the request
Given I have previously loaded offers and lose connectivity, When a refresh fails, Then stale cached offers remain visible with a banner: 'You're offline — showing last updated offers'
Given a screen reader is active, When an empty or error state is displayed, Then the state message and available actions are announced immediately
stories.reasoning: Error paths are essential for production readiness. 2 points: empty state UI + error state + offline cache + retry. Internal sensitivity as no PII involved in error/empty states.

stories.title: Supported City Boundary Enforcement
stories.user_story: As a consumer located outside a supported city, I want to understand that location-based offers are not yet available in my area, so that I have clear expectations and know the service is expanding
acceptance_criteria: Given the platform has defined supported city polygons (e.g., London, Manchester, Birmingham), When my device location falls outside all supported polygons, Then geofence monitoring is suspended and no offer-matching events are generated
Given I am outside a supported city, When I open the Offers tab, Then I see a 'Coming soon to your area' screen with a list of currently supported cities and an option to 'Notify me when available'
Given I tap 'Notify me when available', When I confirm, Then my city interest is recorded and I will receive a push notification when my area is added
Given I travel from an unsupported area into a supported city, When my location enters the city polygon, Then geofence monitoring resumes automatically within 60 seconds
Given a screen reader is active, When the 'Coming soon' screen is displayed, Then the supported city list and notification opt-in are fully navigable and announced
Then the matching pipeline logs do not contain user PII — only hashed user_id and offer_id for debugging
stories.regulatory_linkage: UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) — purpose limitation (location used only to determine city membership, not stored beyond check)
stories.reasoning: Boundary enforcement prevents wasted processing and sets user expectations. 3 points: city polygon check + suspend/resume logic + Coming Soon UI + notify-me registration. Restricted because city-membership check uses real-time location.

stories.title: Geofence Event Delivery Failure Handling
stories.user_story: As a consumer whose device loses connectivity while inside a geofence zone, I want my entry event to be delivered when connectivity resumes, so that I still receive the relevant offer
acceptance_criteria: Given a geofence_entry event is generated while the device has no network connectivity, When connectivity is restored, Then the queued event is delivered to the backend within 10 seconds of reconnection

Given a queued event is older than 15 minutes when connectivity resumes, When evaluating staleness, Then the event is discarded (consumer likely no longer in zone) and not sent to the matching pipeline
Given the backend rejects an event (4xx response), When the rejection occurs, Then the event is not retried and is logged locally for diagnostics
Given the backend is unavailable (5xx/timeout), When delivery fails, Then the device retries with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts, 5s/15s/45s intervals)
Then no queued location events are persisted to device storage in plaintext; events are held in encrypted memory or secure temporary storage only
stories.regulatory_linkage: UK GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) — storage limitation (discard stale events, don't accumulate location history)
stories.reasoning: Error path story for connectivity failures — critical for real-world mobile usage. 2 points: queue + staleness check + retry logic + secure storage. Restricted as queued events contain location data.

stories.title: Geofence Zone Spatial Query Performance
stories.user_story: As a platform operator, I want spatial queries against the zone database to resolve within 50ms at P99, so that the real-time matching pipeline meets its 2-second end-to-end SLA
acceptance_criteria: Given the zone database contains up to 10,000 active zones across all supported cities, When a point-in-polygon query is executed, Then the result is returned within 50ms at P99
Given a new zone is created or updated, When the spatial index is refreshed, Then subsequent queries include the new/updated zone within 5 seconds without full reindex
Given a bulk import of 500+ zones, When the import completes, Then a full GiST index rebuild is triggered and completes within 30 seconds
Given query latency exceeds 50ms at P99 over a 5-minute window, When the threshold is breached, Then a Cloud Monitoring alert fires to the on-call platform operator
Then all spatial queries use parameterised inputs to prevent SQL injection against the PostGIS layer
Then geofence event data older than 24 hours is automatically purged from the processing pipeline per data minimization
stories.reasoning: Performance story ensures the spatial layer doesn't bottleneck the pipeline. 3 points: GiST optimization + incremental reindex + bulk rebuild + monitoring/alerting + parameterised queries. Restricted as zone data is location-sensitive.

stories.title: Offer Matching Pipeline Dead-Letter and Observability
stories.user_story: As a platform operator, I want failed or timed-out matching events to be captured in a dead-letter queue with full observability, so that I can diagnose issues and ensure no consumer events are silently lost
acceptance_criteria: Given a matching event exceeds the 2-second SLA or throws an unhandled exception, When the failure occurs, Then the event is routed to a Pub/Sub dead-letter topic with original payload, failure reason, and timestamp
Given events accumulate in the dead-letter topic, When the count exceeds 10 in a 5-minute window, Then a P2 alert fires to the on-call operator via Cloud Monitoring

Given I am a platform operator viewing the observability dashboard, When I inspect pipeline health, Then I see real-time metrics: throughput (events/sec), P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, and dead-letter depth
Given a dead-lettered event is investigated, When I trigger a manual replay, Then the event is re-injected into the pipeline with a replay flag (preventing duplicate offer delivery)
Then all pipeline logs include correlation_id (trace_id) linking geofence event → matching → dispatch for end-to-end tracing via Cloud Trace

architecture_kb_sections: kb-L0-lloyds-enterprise-architecture §3.3 (Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Trace, Cloud Logging)

stories.reasoning: Operational resilience story — ensures no silent data loss in the critical path. 3 points: dead-letter routing + alerting + dashboard + manual replay + distributed tracing. Restricted as dead-lettered events contain consumer location context.
